text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bunds pared gains but remained up on the day in futures-dominated trade buoyed by news Bonn plans no further Bund issue this year. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 98.95, up 0.27 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts locked in a 15/32 gain on Thursday, dragged higher by buoyant U.S. Treasuries which were thrilled with durable goods data showing a 3.1 percent fall in orders in August. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-19/32, up 19/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures rallied to a new contract high on Thursday on the back of a supportive U.S. bond market, hopes for lower interest rates in Europe and relief that no long-dated Bunds will be issued in the fourth quarter. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 124.78, up 0.26 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets and the lira reined in their earlier enthusiasm to stand around 50 basis points higher on the day, instead of up at the record 120.98 peak set on the December LIFFE future. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 121.75, up 1.80 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were higher at midday after a weaker-than-expected August durable goods orders report encouraged the view that the Federal Reserve would leave interest rates untouched for the rest of the year. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-26/32, up 19/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.88 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond futures closed near the day's low in Tokyo, due to long liquidation and large-lot selling by a major U.S. brokerage firm. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 121.81, down 0.47 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market continued in top gear as bullish sentiment continued to boost issuance. The sterling sector saw further supply -- the EIB raised 200 million stg, while Northern Rock raised 150 million stg. Cades launched an expected 12 bln French franc domestic bond which matures in July 2005. In dollars, GECC set a $250 million six-year bond while in the emerging market sector, Acesita set a $150 million eight-year bond which has a put after five years. Australian dollars, guilders and marks were also tapped.
